artifact: eCourts source/parser acceptance fixtures — NEW2, independent of the implementation
status: NO LIVE REQUEST HAS BEEN MADE. `ecourts_fetch_ledger` holds refusals only, `FQ-ECOURTS-ACTOR` is unanswered, and nothing here fetches anything. These are the questions the first real canary must survive, written before the data exists so they cannot be shaped by it.
why_independent: LCC owns `ecourts-derivation.ts` and its tests. A parser graded only by its author's fixtures is graded on the cases its author thought of. These are NEW2's, they are about SOURCE TRUTH rather than code paths, and every one of them encodes a way a registry page has already misled somebody.

acceptance_questions.question: RAW RESPONSE TRUTH — is the bytes-as-received preserved, hashed, and recoverable independently of whatever the parser made of them?
acceptance_questions.pass: every observation carries `payloadSha256` over the exact bytes, and the bytes are retrievable. A parser change must be re-runnable against the original response without a new request — the grant's daily cap makes re-fetching to re-parse a real cost, not a theoretical one.
acceptance_questions.fail: the raw body is discarded after parsing, or the hash is computed over a normalised form.

acceptance_questions.question: CNR IDENTITY — is the CNR treated as the identity, and is a malformed one refused rather than coerced?
acceptance_questions.pass: a 16-character CNR matching the registry's own shape is the join key; anything else sets `extractionState` and yields EXTRACTION_UNUSABLE.
acceptance_questions.fail: matching on case number and year, which repeat across establishments; or upper-casing/space-stripping a CNR into validity.

acceptance_questions.question: NEXT-DATE INTERPRETATION — is a next date an observation of what a page showed, never a prediction of what will happen?
acceptance_questions.pass: NEXT_DATE_OBSERVED carries the date and the observation it came from. A later page showing a different date yields NEXT_DATE_CHANGED, not a silent overwrite.
acceptance_questions.fail: a single mutable `next_hearing_date` column on the matter that the newest fetch overwrites.

acceptance_questions.question: BENCH FIELDS — is `bench` the judges who sat, and never the establishment code?
acceptance_questions.fail: `bench = 'phhc'` or `courtNumber` written into the coram. This exact confusion already shipped 40,705 rows in the corpus (migration 0040) and it is the same word for two things.

acceptance_questions.question: LISTING SEMANTICS — LISTED is not HEARD.
acceptance_questions.pass: appearing on a cause list yields LISTED_OBSERVED and nothing else. There is no projection meaning the hearing happened, because a website is not a courtroom.
acceptance_questions.fail: any surface that tells an advocate a hearing took place because the case was listed.

acceptance_questions.question: ORDER-LINK SEMANTICS — an order link is not a fresh order and is not a document.
acceptance_questions.pass: ORDER_AVAILABILITY_CANDIDATE, carrying the reference only, joined to nothing in the corpus until the document itself is fetched and verified.
acceptance_questions.fail: treating the appearance of a link as evidence that an order was passed on the listing date, or auto-linking it to a judgment by case number.

acceptance_questions.question: DUPLICATE TRANSITIONS — does re-reading the same unchanged page produce a change?
acceptance_questions.pass: two fetches of an unchanged page produce one state, not two transitions. Idempotence is on content, not on fetch count.
acceptance_questions.fail: a notification per fetch — which, at the grant's 100/hour, is a notification storm rather than a product.

grant_conditions_these_must_respect.note: every fixture above assumes the request that produced it was itself permitted, ledgered and rate-limited. An acceptance suite that passes on responses obtained outside the grant has tested the wrong thing.
